news.title: How south west London watched a World Cup from across the Atlantic
news.lede: For a tournament played four or five thousand miles away, the 2026 World Cup left a surprisingly deep mark on south west London. From packed beer gardens in Wandsworth to living rooms in Kingston where the football did not kick off until the children were long asleep, the summer’s football rearranged the rhythm of daily life across the boroughs in ways a European tournament never quite manages. A World Cup on the other side of the Atlantic is a different creature, and the way local communities adapted to it says something about how football is actually lived here. The tournament ran from the middle of June to the middle of July, staged across the United States, Canada and Mexico, and the geography changed everything about how it was consumed.

news.title: FIFA sacks Chief Operating Officer over Infantino World Cup sell-off criticism
news.lede: FIFA’s chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, has left the organisation following weeks of public criticism directed at president Gianni Infantino’s now-abandoned plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. FIFA confirmed the working relationship between FIFA and Lamour as chief operating officer ended on August 17, 2026. Staff were informed of the departure in an email from Secretary General Mattias Grafstrom, who said the organisation and Lamour had “agreed to part ways.” A letter sent to FIFA vice presidents and council members added that the decision was made “after careful consideration and with great respect for Kevin, both personally and professionally.”

news.title: Fifa chief SACKED by Gianni Infantino weeks after blasting shameless World Cup sell-off plot
news.lede: THE first Fifa chief to bravely blast Gianni Infantino’s World Cup selling scheme has been sacked. Kevin Lamour was the world football governing body’s chief operating officer. However, he put his neck out to slam the money-grabbing plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other tournaments to raise £20billion. Lamour, 46, insisted Infantino acted alone and was willing to lose his job over his bold comments.

news.title: World Cup stake sale plan | One more FIFA official resigns as crisis escalates
news.lede: FIFA's chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, has left his role at the game's global governing body just weeks after saying its president, Gianni Infantino, had deceived staff with his World Cup sell-off plan. FIFA confirmed Lamour's exit in a statement to multiple media outlets, saying, "FIFA can confirm that the working relationship between FIFA and Kevin Lamour as FIFA's Chief Operating Officer has ended on 17 August 2026. "FIFA thanks Kevin for his two years of service and wishes him the best of luck for the future. No further comment will be made on the matter." .'

news.title: Nigeria fire Super Falcons boss Justine Madugu as World Cup dream turns into a nightmare
news.lede: The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has sacked Super Falcons coach Justine Madugu after the team failed to qualify for the Women's World Cup for the first time in history. An investigative committee has been launched to examine the collapse, while the NFF leadership faces potential removal ahead of September's elections. NFF has dismissed Super Falcons coach Madugu and his entire technical crew with immediate effect. The decision follows Nigeria's failure to qualify for the FIFA Women's World Cup for the first time in history.

news.title: World Cup Stars Bringing Their Form Back to Club Football
news.lede: The 2026 World Cup did not leave every player in the same condition. Some returned to Europe needing recovery after a demanding tournament; others came back with confidence, match rhythm and strong individual performances behind them. Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland, Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham belong firmly in the second group. That momentum is already influencing expectations around the new club season.
